deep.reconstruction:
Context: Schatten classes L^p(H) for 0<p<1. Write S_p(A)=Σ s_i(A)^p = Tr|A|^p and ||A||_p = S_p(A)^{1/p}. The previous page proves that ||·||_p is a norm for p≥1 by duality (formula (7)). It notes that this argument fails for p<1. Formula (4) is evidently the p-subadditivity S_p(A+B) ≤ S_p(A)+S_p(B) for 0<p<1. Lemma 1 (previous page) states: for α_i ≥ 0 and f(z)=∏(1+α_i z), Σ α_i^p = (p sin πp/π)∫_0^∞ log f(x) x^{-1-p} dx. This rests on ∫_0^∞ log(1+u) u^{-1-p} du = π/(p sin πp).

This page:
(i) Corollary. For A trace class, let M_A(r)=sup_{|z|=r}|det(1+zA)|. Then S_p(A) = (p sin πp/π)∫_0^∞ log M_{|A|}(r) r^{-1-p} dr. Proof: take f(z)=det(1+z|A|), whose zeros are -1/s_i. Since |A| ≥ 0, M_{|A|}(r)=f(r).
(ii) Proof of (4). Write S_p(A+B)=S_p(|A+B|) and apply (9). Then use the (unproved, cited as '(formule ...)') inequality det(1+r|A+B|) ≤ det(1+r|A|) det(1+r|B|), i.e. (10) M_{|A+B|} ≤ M_{|A|} M_{|B|}. Taking logs and integrating against r^{-1-p} dr gives subadditivity. General A,B ∈ L^p follow by approximation, which is not mentioned.
(iii) Start of remark 2). Proving formula (5) needs, as far as he knows, a complicated method. He sets up, for compact A with eigenvalues λ_i, the eigenvalue sum Σ|λ_i|^p. A struck-out line anticipates the power trick s_p(A)=s_{p/n}(A^n). (5) is apparently Weyl's inequality Σ|λ_i|^p ≤ S_p(A).

The next page completes (iii). Jensen's formula gives Σ|λ_i|^p ≤ p²∫ log M_A(r) r^{-1-p} dr. With M_A ≤ M_{|A|} and (9), this yields Σ|λ_i|^p ≤ (pπ/sin pπ) S_p(A). The constant is then removed by passing to A^n, using Hölder S_{p/n}(A^n) ≤ S_p(A), and letting n→∞, where pπ/sin pπ → 1. This is an amplification ('power') trick.

Purpose: an analytic, entire-function / Fredholm-determinant approach to the quasi-normed ideals L^p, p<1. It belongs to the circle of ideas of Produits tensoriels topologiques and La théorie de Fredholm (eigenvalues of nuclear operators).
errors: Key gap: the inequality det(1+r|A+B|) ≤ det(1+r|A|)det(1+r|B|) is invoked as '(formule ...)' without proof. It is true but not elementary. Via polar decomposition it reduces to |det(1+X+Y)| ≤ det(1+|X|)det(1+|Y|) (Seiler–Simon 1975). Equivalently it is the Rotfel'd inequality for the concave function log(1+t) (Rotfel'd ~1967–69). It does NOT follow from Ky Fan's weak majorization, which only handles convex increasing functions. So the proof of (4) is complete only modulo this nontrivial inequality.
M_A(r) should be defined with a modulus, sup_{|z|=r}|det(1+zA)|.
The zeros of det(1+z|A|) are the negatives of the inverses of the eigenvalues, -1/s_i, not the inverses. This is harmless.
The corollary is stated for A ∈ L^1. Deducing (4) for general A,B ∈ L^p requires an unmentioned approximation step.
The label (10) is reused on the next page for a different inequality.

ideas.what: Mellin-type identity Σα_i^p = (p sin πp/π)∫ log∏(1+α_i x) x^{-1-p}dx applied to Fredholm determinants: S_p(A) = (p sin πp/π)∫ log det(1+r|A|) r^{-1-p} dr
ideas.modern_name: Integral representation of t^p (0<p<1) via log(1+rt); log-determinant formula for Schatten quasi-norms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (entire function theory; standard integral representation of operator-concave functions)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related material in 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956) / Produits tensoriels topologiques (1955); unsure

ideas.what: p-subadditivity S_p(A+B) ≤ S_p(A)+S_p(B) for Schatten classes, 0<p<1, reduced to a determinant inequality
ideas.modern_name: p-triangle inequality for Schatten quasi-norms (Rotfel'd / McCarthy inequality)
ideas.usually_credited_to: S. Yu. Rotfel'd (1967–69); C. McCarthy (1967); later R. C. Thompson

ideas.modern_name: Seiler–Simon determinant inequality / Rotfel'd inequality for f(t)=log(1+t)
ideas.usually_credited_to: E. Seiler and B. Simon (1975); Rotfel'd

ideas.what: Weyl eigenvalue inequality Σ|λ_i|^p ≤ Σ s_i^p via Jensen bound plus an n-th power amplification trick to remove the constant pπ/sin pπ (prepared here, executed next page)
ideas.modern_name: Weyl's inequality; amplification/'tensor power' style trick
ideas.where_published: Possibly analogous arguments in 'La théorie de Fredholm' (1956); unsure

missed.claim: In 1953 Grothendieck reduced the p-subadditivity of Schatten quasi-norms (0<p<1) to the multiplicative determinant inequality det(1+r|A+B|) ≤ det(1+r|A|)det(1+r|B|), through an exact log-determinant integral formula. He thereby isolates the statement later proved as Rotfel'd's inequality (late 1960s) and the Seiler–Simon inequality (1975). Whether he had a proof is unclear: the justification is a blank '(formule ...)'.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: it shows the determinant route to the p<1 Schatten triangle inequality was envisaged about 15 years before Rotfel'd and McCarthy. If an earlier page of the archive contains a proof of the cited 'formule', that would predate Seiler–Simon.

missed.claim: The page leaves the crucial determinant inequality unjustified. Grothendieck also says he knows only a 'complicated method' for the eigenvalue inequality (5), suggesting the analytic program was not polished or published.
missed.quote: Pour prouver la formule (5), je ne connais qu'une méthode compliquée.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: modern proofs exist (Horn/Weyl via exterior powers; Rotfel'd, Thompson, Bourin–Uchiyama). This is of mainly historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: The individual ingredients are classical or later-standard (Weyl's inequality, the Schatten p<1 triangle inequality, the Mellin-type integral identity). What is mildly notable is Grothendieck's 1953 analytic strategy, which explicitly reduces S_p subadditivity to the determinant inequality later known as Seiler–Simon/Rotfel'd. This predates the published results, but he leaves that key step unproved.
transcription_corrections: M_A(r) = sup_{|z|=r} |det(1+zA)| (modulus intended; the image omits bars).
The deleted line reads roughly 'si A est hermitien positif, et si A ∈ L^p(H)', followed by 'et 0<p<1'.
'dont les zéros sont les inverses des valeurs propres de |A|': the reading is uncertain, and mathematically the zeros are the negatives of the inverses.
In the long display, the denominators of the two integrals are r^{1+p}; the image's 'r^{1+r}' is a slip of the pen.
The struck-out heading before '2)' looks like 'Remarque'.
The struck-out final lines mention 'S_p(A) = S_{p/n}(A^n)' for 'tout entier n>0', i.e. the power trick carried out on the next page.
